title: Pausing any single token blocks ALL claims via DoS — inconsistency between claim() and calculateClaimAmount()
description: claim() at line 589 reverts with TokenIsPaused() for ANY paused token in the strategy iteration loop. But calculateClaimAmount() at line 803 uses 'continue' to skip paused tokens and returns a non-zero claimable amount. This inconsistency means pausing a single low-value token (expected admin action during depeg events) blocks ALL yield distribution across ALL strategies. Off-chain callers including ClaimArbitrage bots read calculateClaimAmount() which reports available yield, then claim() reverts.
impact: Pausing a single token (expected admin behavior during depeg) prevents claiming yield from ALL strategies. calculateClaimAmount() returns misleading values. Blocks ClaimArbitrage and all individual claimers. Yield accumulates indefinitely until the problematic token is unpaused.
attackPath: 1. Admin pauses one token via pauseToken() due to a depeg event
2. calculateClaimAmount() returns non-zero value (skips paused tokens with continue)
3. ClaimArbitrage bot sees positive yield, calibrates parameters, calls execute()
4. Step 3: sya.claim() iterates strategies, hits the paused token at line 589
6. All yield remains unclaimed until admin unpauses the problematic token
recommendation: Change claim() to skip paused tokens with 'continue' (matching calculateClaimAmount() behavior). If all-or-nothing semantics are intentional, update calculateClaimAmount() to also revert when any token is paused, so view and state-changing functions are consistent.
